correctness.rationale: Read assigned RESULT.md and exact-rational verify_degrees.py. Given an existing degree-k vertex, the next duplicate links to it with conditional probability (k+q)/n (parent one of its k neighbors or the vertex with a true-twin Bernoulli q). The founder count follows the classical Pólya recursion. For a uniform vertex, expected counts of old degree-k vertices plus the newborn parent degree+Bernoulli(q) yield h_{n+1}(k)=[(n+1-k-2q)h_n(k)+(k-1+2q)h_n(k-1)]/(n+1). This is exactly beta-binomial with a=2q,b=2(1−q). Initial n=1 and boundary k=0,n−1 are handled, n arbitrary. The beta mixture gives the stated variance and weak limits. Independently enumerated full probability laws of actual labeled recursive graphs at 15 (n,q) cases with n≤5 using exact fractions, verifying BOTH degree laws. No quenched or joint degree-law result claimed.

value.rationale: Vertex degrees are a natural first-order observable in growing random graph models. The all-n finite distribution with doubled beta parameters and its exactly flat q=1/2 case distinguish typical and founder age laws, giving useful interpretable marginal information not merely a table or a graphon existence statement.

final_claim: In uniform-parent recursive cographs, join probability q∈(0,1), founder degree is BetaBin(n−1;q,1−q) and conditional-uniform sampled-vertex degree is BetaBin(n−1;2q,2−2q). At q=1/2 the latter is exactly uniform over all n degrees at every finite n. Stated means, variances and two beta weak limits follow.
limitations: Annealed typical/founder degree distributions, not almost-sure empirical distribution, joint degrees, or model novelty.
